errors.problem: In the comparative and superlative lessons, مِنْ is the key word: 'than' after a comparative (أَكْبَرُ مِنْ = bigger than) and 'one of' before a superlative plus a plural (مِنْ أَجْمَلِ الْأَمَاكِن). The tap gloss is always 'from' (مِنَ in day 63 = 'of, from'). So quiz d61q1 'What does this mean? أَكْبَرُ مِنْ' taps as 'bigger · from', and the correct answer of d63q5 (مِنْ أَجْمَلِ الْأَمَاكِن) taps as 'from · the most beautiful (of) · the places'. The segs say 'than' and 'of, among' correctly. 17 taps in total.
errors.fix: مِنْ=from; than (after a comparative); one of (before a superlative)
errors.alsoChange: same for مِنَ (day 63 intro: 'of, from; than')

errors.problem: Still there from round 1. Day 66 teaches مُسَافِر as the active participle 'travelling, away on a trip' (summary: 'say who is away, travelling…'; quiz d66q1 answer 'travelling'). The tap gives only the noun sense 'passenger, traveller', which is not among the quiz options. glossary-auto-2: مُسَافِر = passenger, traveller (m).

Round 1 corrected the imperative gloss to 'uses (past)', which contradicts itself: a present tense marked as past. اِسْتَعْمَلَ is the Form X past tense 'he used' (the summary prose says 'اِسْتَعْمَلَ (used)', and the dialogue seg says 'and (he) used'). Neighbouring taps follow the '(he) studied / (he) met' style. glossary-auto-1: اِسْتَعْمَلَ = uses (past).

One o'clock is الْوَاحِدَة, literally 'the one': it is the only hour that does not use an ordinal. 'The first' is الْأُولَى. The gloss teaches a wrong equation (wāḥida = first), while the parallel segs التَّاسِعَة = 'the ninth' and الرَّابِعَة = 'the fourth' are correct. glossary-auto-1 has the same wrong gloss: الْوَاحِدَة = the first (f): one o'clock.

The culture note says that colleagues and managers are called أُسْتَاذ / أُسْتَاذَة 'even if they are not teachers', but the tap on أُسْتَاذَة (from the hand glossary) says only 'teacher (f)'. The masculine tap in the same line gives 'professor; teacher; Mr (title)', and the day-64 seg says 'madam (polite address for a woman)'.
errors.alsoChange: glossary-hand.txt: أُسْتَاذَة ⟶ teacher (f); Mrs, madam (polite title)

Jordanian is still spelt two ways: أُرْدُنِيَّة (no shadda) and الْأُرْدُنِّيّ (shadda). Pick one.
وَكَانَتْ مَدِينَة غَنِيَّة: the predicate of kāna is accusative (مَدِينَةً غَنِيَّةً). The house style omits tanwīn on ة, so this is left as a note, but here it hides the kāna rule.
The note for سَعَدَ says only '(wrong — correct: sāʿada, helped)'. That is fine, though سَعِدَ (be happy) is a real verb; the note could say 'not Form III'.
أَحْسَنُ before an indefinite singular is glossed 'the best (of)'. Elsewhere the course uses 'the best (before a noun)' for the same construction (أَفْضَلُ رِحْلَة). Harmless; aligning would help.

summary: I read the whole days-61-70 export: every Arabic line with its harakat, case endings, agreement and verb forms; every translation and literal, seg, tap gloss, quiz answer key and mistake card; and the mistake-note glossary entries used by this chunk. I checked that the round-1 fixes are in place: دَرَّسَ, تَرُدَّ, قَرِيبًا, الْكِتَابَة, ل as a letter, مُدِير, the iḍāfa vowels (مَدِينَةُ جِبَال, كَلِمَةِ دِيوَان, كَلِمَةِ مَدْرَسَة), اجْتِمَاعًا, shāy, li-Sāmī / wa-Laylā, wa-ttaṣala and tāʾ marbūṭa in prose are all fixed. The Arabic itself remains clean: numerals, duals, subjunctives after أَنْ, kāna/laysa predicates and hamza seats (تَقْرَئِيهَا, أَخْطَائِكُمَا, أَسْئِلَتِكُمْ) are correct, and all 70 quiz answer keys are right with no second correct option. 10 errors, 1 major and 9 minor. Six are glosses: أَكْبَرُ is still tapped 'bigger' in superlative phrases, which points to the wrong option of d62q1 (the major one); مِنْ is tapped 'from' where it means 'than' or 'one of'; مُسَافِر is still tapped 'passenger'; اِسْتَعْمَلَ now shows the self-contradictory 'uses (past)'; the seg الْوَاحِدَة = 'the first'; أُسْتَاذَة = 'teacher (f)' in a note about non-teachers. Two are minor vocalisation points: a mid-sentence waṣla with a kasra, and الْيَوْم without its fatha at the start of a clause. Two are engine points: a bare ئ is still dropped, and الْعَيْن is capitalised. Tap glosses: I checked 696 (283 distinct word=gloss pairs across 276 tap lines); 29 were wrong or misleading in context (17 مِنْ, 5 أَكْبَرُ, 4 مُسَافِر, 2 اِسْتَعْمَلَ, 1 أُسْتَاذَة). Pattern: when a form has only one glossary entry, the lesson-day mechanism cannot choose the sense the day teaches, so the remaining problems are single-sense glossary entries for words this chunk uses in a new sense.
